LESSON: GERMAN ACCENT MARKS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: GERMAN BRAILLE
Topic 9.1: German Accent Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers German Accent Marks, part of GERMAN BRAILLE in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How do you distinguis h accent marks from letters of alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify accent marks in German braille by naming the dots correctly

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of German Accent Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read out words with accent marks in German braille

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of German Accent Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. write accent marks in German braille

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of German Accent Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of accent marks in German braille. Learners be guided to: • Identify accent marks in German braille used on the same word in German braille by feeling and naming the dots on braille cards • Read out words with accent marks in braille • Write words with accent marks in braille • Practise reading and writing words and sentences with accent marks in German braille in groups. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on German Accent Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as learners work together in groups while practicing

reading and writing words and sentences with German accent marks in braille.

• Learning to learn: This is developed as learners look for more words with German accent marks to improve

their reading skills in German braille.
